clues: This city lies on the banks of the greatest river in the land, in the southeast of its state. Low bluffs lift it just above the wide water.
Winters here are mild and summers are hot and humid, with heavy rain through the year. Damaging winds and tornadoes can strike in any season.
In 1846, state lawmakers picked this river town as the new capital. It took the place of a great port town down the river.
Long ago, explorers found a red pole standing here. It marked the boundary between the hunting grounds of two tribes.
The governor of Louisiana works in this town by the river. The men and women who make state laws meet in the tall capitol here.
